metric.why: A facility can have enough total cooling and still starve individual racks; airflow and pressure sensors find recirculation, bypass, and leaks that temperature averages hide.
metric.definition: Cubic feet per minute delivered through the room or containment system, and the pressure differential that drives it through equipment rather than around it.

reading.body:
Cooling capacity is a room-level number, but cooling delivery is a rack-level one. Airflow and static pressure show whether cold air actually reaches the equipment or moves around it.

Temperature and humidity readings, the sibling metric here, are averages over a space. Averages hide recirculation, bypass, and leaks, because a room can hold its target temperature while specific racks draw air that never passed through the cooling system. Static pressure is the part that decides direction: air follows the path of least resistance, and a containment system with adequate total cubic feet per minute can still push most of it around equipment rather than through it. For AI specifically, this matters because the failure mode is per-rack, not per-room. A facility with enough total cooling can still starve individual racks, and the racks that starve are the dense ones.

What this data does not cover is any measurement. There are no thresholds, no readings, no counts of facilities, and no indication of how often airflow or pressure is sampled. It sits alongside two other cooling metrics, liquid coolant temperature and flow rate, and hot and cold aisle temperature and humidity, which together describe cooling as a delivery problem rather than a capacity problem. Nothing here speaks to power draw, power supply, or the grid, so it cannot support any claim about compute scaling beyond the cooling layer it describes.
